learn.title: The shape of $x^2$
learn.body: A quadratic function has the form $y=ax^2+bx+c$ with $a\ne0$. Its graph is a parabola, a smooth U-shaped curve. If $a>0$ it opens up, and if $a<0$ it opens down.

learn.title: Key points
learn.body: The vertex is the turning point. The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through it: $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$. The $y$-intercept is $c$, because $x=0$ leaves only $c$.

learn.title: A table confirms it
learn.body: For $y=x^2-4x+3$ the values at $x=0,1,2,3,4$ are $3,0,-1,0,3$. They mirror around $x=2$, which is the axis of symmetry.
Points at equal distance from the axis have equal heights. Use one side to get the other for free.

questions.explanation: The coefficient of $x^2$ is $a=1$, which is positive, so the parabola opens up.
Here $a=-2$ is negative, so the curve opens downward.

questions.prompt: The point where a parabola turns is called the \_\_
questions.explanation: It is the lowest point if the parabola opens up, or the highest point if it opens down.

questions.prompt: The axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$. For $y=x^2-4x+3$, find it.
For $y=x^2-4x+3$, find the $y$-value of the vertex.

questions.explanation: Here $b=0$, so the axis is $x=0$. At $x=0$, $y=4$.

questions.prompt: Match each fact with what it tells you.
questions.explanation: Four quick facts that sketch any parabola.
$9-6-3=0$. So 3 is where the graph meets the $x$-axis.
